scope.title: Fillet and chamfer feature parity audit
scope.baseline: OCCT V7_9_3 source inventory plus the recorded Truck/Pieza revisions. Includes 3D, 2D, related workflows and all textual candidates under the discovery rules.
scope.meaning_of_all: Every dedicated test-grid entry, matching registered test/helper, discovered blend command and retained reference in this pinned checkout. This is not a claim about all mathematical configurations or current/future OCCT releases.
scope.execution: The OCCT case corpus has not been executed or paired here. Targeted Truck regression results are recorded on capability entries; case-level comparisons remain unverified.
scope.mapping: Capability assessments describe observable outcomes supported or restricted by reviewed source evidence. Per-case tags and links are automated hints; they do not prove Truck handles that fixture.
scope.objective: Achieve at least OCCT-level fillet/chamfer capabilities and robustness for equivalent modeling tasks in Truck/Pieza.
scope.equivalence: Judge the requested geometry, dimensions, validity, editing behavior and practical performance. Different APIs, algorithms, languages, surface representations and internal operation sequences are acceptable. Missing a corresponding OCCT method is not evidence of a feature gap.

status_definitions.implemented-with-tests: The stated capability has an implementation and relevant assertions, through any equivalent construction. Executed checks are recorded separately where available; broader OCCT case parity remains unverified.
status_definitions.partial: Some configurations have supporting evidence; others have known restrictions or remain unverified. Read the outcome and scope before treating any specific case as a gap.
status_definitions.behavior-difference: The inspected constructions produce different physical constraints or behavior for the same nominal input. Check whether parameter conversion or another existing route provides equivalent results before declaring a capability gap.
status_definitions.app-limitation: An observed product restriction prevents expressing or using a capability. An internal pipeline difference alone is not sufficient evidence.
status_definitions.unverified: The requested outcome has not been established from the inspected evidence. Absence of an OCCT-style API does not establish lack of capability.
status_definitions.reference-only: An OCCT implementation choice retained for investigation. It is not itself a feature requirement or parity deficit.

validation_contract: Express each case as a modeling task: input geometry, physical selection, intended radius/distances/angle, termination and expected result. Identify the same physical entities without relying on ordinal edge IDs across kernels.

Accept any Truck/Pieza construction that satisfies the task, including parameter conversion and composed operations. Require equivalent editing intent and automation; a manually sculpted lookalike does not establish a parametric feature.

API names, signatures, call counts, solver strategy, patch representation and face counts are not parity requirements. Internal differences matter only through observable correctness, robustness, editing or performance.
Record operation failure, crash/timeout, invalid output and valid output separately. A harness expected failure is not a working blend; successful return alone is not proof of correctness.

Validate contact radius/distances/angle, tangency where required, orientation, closed topology/mesh, material membership and global self-intersection independently. Check open-shell tasks against their own boundary contract.
Compare shape and dimensions within explicit tolerances, with volume as a supplementary check. Different valid topology decompositions are acceptable.

Preserve unchanged input on failure; verify persistent selections after upstream edits, STEP round trips and downstream modeling. These outcomes do not require matching OCCT history or diagnostic methods.
Use analytic expectations where available; OCCT supplies cases and comparative evidence, not an infallible oracle or a ceiling on supported behavior.
Record versions, tolerances, physical selection, runtime and fixture hash with results. Practical latency matters, but matching OCCT timing exactly is not required.

families.title: Constant-radius planar fillets
families.occt_scope: Constant-radius contours with analytic special cases.
families.truck_scope: Convex and concave local planar constructions have independent volume and mesh regressions.
families.next_case: Pair box, wedge, tetrahedron and cavity cases; compare contact radius and retained volume.
families.required_outcome: Round selected planar-solid edges to the requested constant radius, for convex and concave material, while preserving a valid solid.

families.title: Variable radius along a tangent chain
families.occt_scope: Linear, interpolated and general radius laws.
families.truck_scope: Kernel tests cover variable-radius chains; the physical profile must be translated to its per-edge parameterization. Pieza currently stores one radius per feature, so product-level variable-radius intent remains limited.
families.next_case: Use unequal edge lengths, split an edge, and compare the same physical radius law; include varying derivatives.
families.required_outcome: Create a smooth blend whose radius follows the requested physical profile along an entire connected chain, including unequal-length and split edges.

families.title: Different radii meeting at a corner
families.occt_scope: Per-edge/contour radii and general corner filling.
families.truck_scope: Equal-radius joined corners are covered. The inspected multi-edge entry point accepts one common radius, but this alone does not prove unequal-radius corners impossible through other constructions. A valid unequal-radius joined result has not been established.
families.next_case: Three edges at a corner with radii 1, 2 and 3, convex then mixed concavity. Try existing joint and composed constructions; judge the resulting contacts, continuity and solid validity.
families.required_outcome: Create a valid joined corner where incident edge fillets have different specified radii, with the intended contacts and continuity.

families.title: Tapered radius reaching zero
families.occt_scope: Singular-corner machinery exists; acceptance of a particular zero-radius law needs execution.
families.truck_scope: Chain validation rejects radius values at or below zero, including endpoints.
families.next_case: Sweep a positive radius down to zero at an endpoint and record each kernel result without presuming OCCT success.
families.required_outcome: Taper a blend continuously to zero radius at an endpoint without leaving an invalid seam or degenerate solid.

families.title: Fillet section representation choices
families.occt_scope: Rational, quasi-angular and polynomial section representations.
families.truck_scope: Truck chooses analytic or procedural surfaces internally. Matching the OCCT representation selector is not required; retain this topic only to investigate accuracy, interoperability or performance differences.
families.next_case: Investigate representations only when an accuracy, STEP, downstream modeling or performance failure is observed. Do not add a selector solely to mirror OCCT.
families.required_outcome: No independent representation-selector requirement. The resulting shape must satisfy geometric accuracy and downstream use regardless of its internal representation.

families.title: Smoothness within and between blend surfaces
families.occt_scope: Configurable internal C0/C1/C2 and support angular tolerance; this is not a promise of G2 support-face blending.
families.truck_scope: Truck has construction-specific smoothness contracts, including deliberately creased two-edge miters. Lack of a continuity-setting method does not establish a gap; evaluate the smoothness required for each result.
families.next_case: Choose a corner or chain with a specified smoothness requirement, then measure internal joins and support-face tangency separately in each output.
families.required_outcome: Achieve the required smoothness within blend surfaces and across their joins; distinguish that from tangency to the support faces.

families.title: Equal-distance chamfers
families.occt_scope: Symmetric chamfers propagated along contours.
families.truck_scope: Planar neighborhoods, nonconvex corners and selected cylinder lips are covered.
families.next_case: Pair simple OCCT fixtures with planar convex and concave solids.
families.required_outcome: Bevel selected edges by equal specified setbacks on both supports, including convex and concave material.

families.title: Unequal chamfer distances and side identity
families.occt_scope: Two distances with an explicit reference face.
families.truck_scope: Per-edge distance pairs and wire direction define the two sides; the app translates named face order.
families.next_case: Reverse wire and face storage order and swap distances; verify contact dimensions.
families.required_outcome: Bevel with independently specified setbacks on the intended two support faces; orientation or storage order must not silently exchange them.

families.title: Distance-and-angle chamfers
families.occt_scope: Explicit distance and angle mode.
families.truck_scope: The existing two-distance construction can express some equivalent planar chamfers after converting the intended angle and setback. That conversion, curved-support behavior and parametric edit semantics need validation; an AddDA-style method is unnecessary.
families.next_case: Convert setback and angle into two support distances on a non-right-angle wedge and validate the result after changing the wedge angle. Then check a curved support where the intended angle must remain controlled.
families.required_outcome: Produce a chamfer with the requested setback and angle, including non-right-angle supports, using any equivalent parameterization.

families.title: Constant-throat chamfers
families.occt_scope: Symmetric constant-throat section constraint.
families.truck_scope: No constant-throat result has been established. Check whether existing distance-based constructions, with derived parameters, satisfy the same throat constraint before identifying new kernel work.
families.next_case: Recreate bug28828_8 and bug28828_10 using existing Truck constructions where possible; measure throat along the edge, including changing support curvature.
families.required_outcome: Produce a chamfer whose normal sections maintain the requested throat dimension along the selected edge.

families.title: Constant throat with penetration
families.occt_scope: Penetrating throat uses an offset support to define the section.
families.truck_scope: The penetrating-throat outcome has not been demonstrated. A differently named or composed construction can supply parity if it satisfies the same geometric constraints.
families.next_case: Recreate bug28828_9, bug28828_11 and NURBS bug28828_6; evaluate existing setback or composed constructions against the throat and penetration dimensions.
families.required_outcome: Produce the requested constant-throat chamfer with penetration, satisfying both the throat and offset-support constraints.

families.title: Meaning of distance on curved supports
families.occt_scope: Classic numerical chamfer contacts satisfy a normal-section plane and a guide-to-contact chord distance.
families.truck_scope: Generic Truck contacts use nearest projections of tangent offsets; the same numeric parameter generally gives a different physical setback from OCCT. This is a dimension-convention difference until equivalent inputs or alternate constructions have been tested.
families.next_case: On a radius-2 cylinder, request a physical chord setback of 1. Translate each parameter convention and measure the result; then check varying curvature where a single converted value may be insufficient.
families.required_outcome: Produce the intended measurable setbacks on curved supports after explicitly translating dimension conventions between kernels.

families.title: Plane/cylinder lips and rims
families.occt_scope: Analytic line/circle special cases plus generic walking.
families.truck_scope: Straight axial lips, circular rims, holes and channels have tests; this does not cover all oblique intersections.
families.next_case: Compare convex/concave lips, hole/boss rims, and a tilted plane cutting a cylinder.
families.required_outcome: Blend lips and rims formed by planes and cylinders, for holes, bosses and channels in either material sense.

families.title: Plane/cone and drafted rims
families.occt_scope: Explicit analytic plane/cone cases.
families.truck_scope: Generic surface APIs exist, but complete paired blend coverage of cone angles and apex proximity has not been established.
families.next_case: Cone rims at several draft angles, both material senses, approaching the apex.
families.required_outcome: Blend drafted or conical rims over varying cone angles and near the apex when a valid requested result exists.

families.title: Cylinder/cylinder, sphere, torus and spline support pairs
families.occt_scope: Generic numerical construction extends beyond analytic special cases.
families.truck_scope: Generic rolling-ball surfaces exist. A broad solid-level support-pair matrix has not been established.
families.next_case: Pair each support type with each other type; convex/concave, isolated edge and corner, regular versus near singular.
families.required_outcome: Blend intersections between curved supports, including cylinders, cones, spheres, tori and spline surfaces, with valid contacts and trimmed output.

families.title: Equivalent analytic versus NURBS representations
families.occt_scope: Tests explicitly convert shapes to NURBS before chamfering.
families.truck_scope: Fixed planar spline support recognition in the kernel and straight spline edge grouping in Pieza. The app now keeps B-spline/positive-weight NURBS segments with monotone collinear control polygons in the same junction operation as analytic lines. Planar rim fillets and asymmetric chamfers have regressions; broader representation invariance remains open.
families.next_case: Compare curved support pairs and split faces across analytic/NURBS/STEP representations. Investigate the generic along-wire kernel path separately: the former app routing reached an IntersectionCurve panic instead of returning a diagnostic.
families.required_outcome: Handle equivalent physical geometry consistently when represented analytically, as exact NURBS, with split faces, or after STEP import.
verification: Reproduced UnsupportedGeometry on a valid NURBS-converted drafted rim before the fix; the equivalent analytic fixture passed.

Truck regressions now pass for B-spline/NURBS rims, convex and cavity boundaries, both draft directions, two-edge/full-rim selections, two radii, rotation/translation/scaling, input and selection-order preservation, exact volume, contact radius/tangency and STEP exchange.
Spline cavity-rim chamfers also pass independent volume and STEP checks for both draft directions and both spline representations.

Before the app fix, two selected cubic B-spline cube edges were handled sequentially and panicked inside IntersectionCurve; the analytic control passed. Grouping by segment geometry fixes the selected junction without changing curve representations.

App regressions pass for two-edge/full-rim selections, weighted NURBS and B-spline segments, unequal chamfer side assignments, radius/volume/closed-mesh checks, transforms, scale, reversed selection order and retained names. Bowed, retracing and singular splines are excluded from straight-segment routing.

A STEP-linked NURBS cube supports filleting, document save/load and an upstream height change while retaining body and generated-face references. Output STEP is checked at the documented fitting tolerance, with closed tessellation and independent volume.

App fix committed as 48e8fe2. cargo test --locked -p cad-core --no-fail-fast: 425 passed, 0 failed, 2 existing ignored, including the permanent imported-spline-fillet corpus case and CLI checks. cargo clippy --locked -p cad-core --all-targets completed with warnings in unchanged files.

Broader suite validation found a pre-existing failure in r11_corners::unsupported_junctions_have_distinct_diagnostics: a pyramid chamfer succeeds where the test expects UnsupportedTopology. Reproduced unchanged at parent 7eb2d78d with the same Cargo.lock; the assertion is retained.
These are independently specified Truck/Pieza regression fixtures, not executions of the 1,026 OCCT corpus entries.

families.title: Curved and closed spline spines
families.occt_scope: Closed Bezier/spline spine regressions and general walking.
families.truck_scope: A generic curved-surface test exists; closed spline seam, inflection and tiny-edge variants remain unverified.
families.next_case: Port the six bug30940 cases, including a closed single-edge Bezier spine.
families.required_outcome: Blend along open and closed curved edges, including spline inflections and high curvature, with valid closure and contacts.

families.title: Tangent propagation across support changes
families.occt_scope: Contours propagate along tangent edges and tangent support series.
families.truck_scope: Application propagation checks edge tangents and both face normals; the kernel accepts explicitly supplied chains.
families.next_case: Vary tangency around the threshold and split one support into multiple patches.
families.required_outcome: Round or bevel a tangent chain continuously across edge splits and changes of support face.

families.title: Closed chains and periodic seams
families.occt_scope: Closed/tangent states, periodic surface handling and seam-related regressions, including expected failures.
families.truck_scope: Cylinder-rim seam crossings are tested; broader seam interactions are unverified.
families.next_case: Move cylinder/torus seams through a termination, then repeat with a closed spline edge.
families.required_outcome: Complete a closed blend without gaps or invalid topology, regardless of where periodic seams lie.

families.title: Branching or ambiguous chain selection
families.occt_scope: Contour discovery and endpoint classification.
families.truck_scope: The app explicitly rejects multiple tangent continuation candidates.
families.next_case: A vertex with two geometrically tangent candidates; establish desired selection semantics.
families.required_outcome: Resolve or report ambiguous tangent branches predictably, while allowing the intended explicit path to be selected.

families.title: Open shells and free-boundary terminations
families.occt_scope: Shell input and explicit free-boundary endpoint state.
families.truck_scope: Generic face/shell functions exist, while the app uses solid wrappers requiring closed output.
families.next_case: A two-face open shell ending at a free boundary; separate kernel capability from app scope.
families.required_outcome: Blend open-shell edges and terminate correctly on free boundaries for surface-modeling tasks.

families.title: Single fillet with oblique end faces
families.occt_scope: Intersection with terminating support faces.
families.truck_scope: Exact planar elliptical terminations and selected curved ends are covered.
families.next_case: Acute and obtuse end planes, flipped orientations and very short retained edges.
families.required_outcome: Terminate a blend correctly against oblique end faces while preserving the requested radius and a valid boundary.

families.title: Single blend ending across multiple faces
families.occt_scope: End intersection across face neighborhoods; API documentation retains limitations.
families.truck_scope: Four-valent single-fillet endings and endings on two earlier chamfers have tests.
families.next_case: Use nonplanar multi-face caps and changed seam placement; do not label every four-valent vertex unsupported.
families.required_outcome: Terminate one blend across a neighborhood of several end faces without gaps, overlaps or damage to unrelated geometry.

families.title: Three equal-radius edges with the same concavity
families.occt_scope: Spherical special cases and general three-corner construction.
families.truck_scope: Spherical corners at arbitrary planar angles, including nonconvex bodies and cavity shells.
families.next_case: Pair tetrahedra and oblique reentrant solids, with one, two and three selected edges.
families.required_outcome: Join three equal-radius, same-concavity rounds at a valid corner over general planar support angles.

families.title: Two-edge junction with nonorthogonal supports
families.occt_scope: Intersection and constrained-filling paths.
families.truck_scope: The specialized planar miter path requires perpendicular supports, but the solid-level intersection fallback already handles drafted planar rims. Equal-draft convex/cavity configurations have geometric regressions. The required continuity and more general corner configurations still need case-by-case verification.
families.next_case: Broaden solid-level tests to unequal draft angles and multi-blend configurations, measuring dimensions and junction continuity. Do not infer a missing capability from restrictions in the specialized path alone.
families.required_outcome: Join two selected edge rounds at an oblique corner with the required continuity and preservation of the remaining sharp edge.
verification: An equal-draft analytic rim control passed before kernel changes, including independent volume checks. It was not a missing solid-level feature.

families.title: Mixed convex/concave corner transitions
families.occt_scope: Concavity states distinguish same-side and opposite-side corner configurations.
families.truck_scope: Toroidal fillet patches require the rim face perpendicular to both walls; some remaining mixed combinations reject. Chamfers have planar transitions.
families.next_case: Enumerate each concavity sign pattern, selected subset and oblique support angle.
families.required_outcome: Construct valid transitions where convex and concave blends meet, including oblique support configurations.

families.title: Four or more interacting blends at a vertex
families.occt_scope: General n-corner construction exists, with documented and implementation limitations.
families.truck_scope: The equal-radius multi-edge path rejects general high-valence corners. Single-blend high-valence termination is a different supported case.
families.next_case: Pyramid apex with two, three, four and all incident edges selected.
families.required_outcome: Join four or more interacting blends at a vertex when the requested configuration has a valid solution.

families.title: General curved multi-blend corner filling
families.occt_scope: Constrained patch filling after intersection of blend strips.
families.truck_scope: Exact special junctions exist; generic chain construction does not join several fillets at a vertex.
families.next_case: Cylinder/cone or spline supports meeting at a multi-edge corner, with equal then unequal radii.
families.required_outcome: Close multi-blend corners on general curved supports with valid contact and continuity, independent of patch construction method.

families.title: Contact collapse and singular tips
families.occt_scope: Singular corners and degenerate boundaries are explicitly represented.
families.truck_scope: Equal-radius sequential rim fillets fail by contract. Specific collapsed chamfers are supported.
families.next_case: Sweep second-radius/first-radius through 0.99, 1 and 1.01; compare fillet and chamfer behavior.
families.required_outcome: Handle valid limiting cases where contact curves collapse or tips become singular, with controlled rejection of impossible configurations.

families.title: Disappearing support faces
families.occt_scope: Topology reconstruction can remove/replace entities; this is not a guarantee for every collapse.
families.truck_scope: Touching concave rib rounds can consume a face. Ordinary chamfer construction rejects removing original faces.
families.next_case: A thin support face shrinking to zero and disappearing, with parallel and intersecting rounds.

evidence.find: Sizes that remove an original face

families.required_outcome: Continue valid blending through the disappearance of a support face and reconstruct the remaining material correctly.

families.title: Disappearing unselected edges and blend contacts
families.occt_scope: Corner rebuilding and restricted-boundary handling.
families.truck_scope: Ordinary chamfer construction rejects removing unselected edges or bevel contacts; narrow exceptions exist in specialized rim handling.
families.next_case: Drive the chamfer across the exact limit where one unselected edge vanishes.

evidence.find: an unselected edge, or a bevel contact

families.required_outcome: Continue valid blending when an unselected edge or intermediate blend contact disappears, rebuilding local topology correctly.

families.title: Folded offsets and overlapping blend patches
families.occt_scope: Twisted-surface state and walking checks; failure remains possible.
families.truck_scope: Regular-contact checks reject folded offsets. Rib patch overlap is rejected. No general recovery construction established.
families.next_case: Increase radius through local curvature and overlap limits and require either a valid result or an actionable rejection.
families.required_outcome: Produce a valid result where one exists as offsets fold or blend patches meet; reliably reject invalid or self-intersecting outcomes.

families.title: Contact crossing a trim loop or hole
families.occt_scope: Walking uses domains, restrictions and endpoint intersections; boundary crossing has limitations.
families.truck_scope: Some neighboring patch traversal works; planar contacts approaching holes are rejected.
families.next_case: Put a hole or split trim boundary directly in the contact path, varying clearance across tolerance.
families.required_outcome: Handle blend contacts that reach trim boundaries or holes, producing the intended material boundary or an accurate geometric rejection.

families.title: Distant face/cavity collisions and global self-intersections
families.occt_scope: Local walking and topology construction do not establish universal collision correctness.
families.truck_scope: The public contract excludes distant faces and other boundaries; there is no global blend collision/self-intersection check.
families.next_case: A blend approaching a remote wall or cavity; independently test intersections and material membership in both outputs.

evidence.find: do not perform a global collision

families.required_outcome: Detect or resolve collisions with distant faces and cavities so a successful blend cannot silently leave an invalid or self-intersecting body.

families.title: Reliable contacts near singularities and competing solutions
families.occt_scope: Start-solution failure is distinct from walking failure.
families.truck_scope: Newton/contact routines have guards and failures; branch coverage across complex supports remains unverified.
families.next_case: Multiple possible contact branches, tangent end contacts and seeds near a singularity.
families.required_outcome: Find the intended valid contact solution near singularities and competing branches without unstable branch jumps or false failures.

families.title: Accuracy through rapidly changing curvature
families.occt_scope: Walking controls steps/deflection and approximation tolerances.
families.truck_scope: Adaptive contact sampling and fitting exist; failed inserted samples propagate.
families.next_case: High-curvature spike between initial samples, long/short edge ratios and tight tolerance.
families.required_outcome: Maintain requested geometric accuracy through rapidly changing curvature and unequal feature scales without missed contact failures.

families.title: Pcurve domains, periodic parameters and seam endpoints
families.occt_scope: Dedicated periodic/singular extrema and parameter repairs.
families.truck_scope: Some exact conic seam handling and reversed-curve fixes exist; general paired seam coverage remains open.
families.next_case: Reverse surface parameters and move the seam through the same physical geometry; verify every edge lies on both supports.
families.required_outcome: Keep blend boundaries on both supports and close them correctly when surface parameters, orientations or seam positions change.

families.title: Almost tangent and nearly coplanar edges
families.occt_scope: Angular tolerances and almost-smooth-edge regressions.
families.truck_scope: App propagation uses a fixed normal/tangent dot threshold; coplanar chamfers are rejected.
families.next_case: Sweep dihedral angle and tangent discontinuity across each threshold at multiple scales.
families.required_outcome: Handle nearly tangent and nearly coplanar selections consistently around tolerance thresholds, without invalid output or unstable propagation.

families.title: Near-limit sizes and tiny retained features
families.occt_scope: Tolerance/scale test grids and shape-tolerance assertions.
families.truck_scope: Near-limit box fillet/chamfer regressions retain tiny valid faces. Broader sliver configurations remain unverified.
families.next_case: Sweep just below, at and above size limits; translate far from the origin and repeat at different scales.
families.required_outcome: Retain valid tiny features near blend size limits and reject sizes beyond the valid geometric range consistently across transforms and scales.

families.title: Sequential fillet/chamfer composition
families.occt_scope: Dedicated sequential chamfer grids and composition regressions.
families.truck_scope: Many feature orders are tested; equal-radius sequential rim fillets and general topology transitions remain limited.
families.next_case: Fillet→fillet, fillet→chamfer, chamfer→fillet and chamfer→chamfer with nearby and intersecting selections.
families.required_outcome: Apply successive rounds and bevels to earlier feature results with correct dimensions, valid topology and stable selections.

families.title: Simultaneous straight and curved selections
families.occt_scope: All added contours are passed to one builder with junction construction.
families.truck_scope: Pieza processes straight selections and curved chains in separate sequential groups. That implementation choice is acceptable if it delivers the requested joint geometry and stable selection behavior; an outcome difference has not been demonstrated here.
families.next_case: Apply the same mixed selection in varied enumeration orders. Compare dimensions, junction continuity, validity and edited results; flag only demonstrated failures or differences in those outcomes.
families.required_outcome: Apply one requested selection containing straight and curved edges with the intended joined result, independent of selection enumeration order.

families.title: Blends on Boolean-generated intersections
families.occt_scope: Boolean/blend combinations and regression fixtures.
families.truck_scope: Boolean-created hole rims and channel lips have tests; arbitrary Boolean spline intersections need more coverage.
families.next_case: Pair through/blind holes, rotated channels, tangent cuts and spline intersection edges.
families.required_outcome: Blend physically selected intersection edges created by Boolean operations and preserve valid solid geometry.

families.title: Stable references after topology edits
families.occt_scope: Generated/modified/deleted queries and OCAF recomputation tests.
families.truck_scope: Face ancestry and regression tests support reference persistence through some changes. Coverage after splits, deletions and replacements remains partial; matching OCCT history-query methods is unnecessary.
families.next_case: Upstream edit after a face splits/disappears; re-resolve every selected edge and generated face.
families.required_outcome: Keep downstream references attached to their intended geometry after upstream edits split, replace or remove blend topology.

families.title: Closed meshes, STEP and downstream modeling
families.occt_scope: Shape, property, tolerance and downstream operation checks across the corpus.
families.truck_scope: Common blend checks cover topology, meshes, volume, STEP and selected Boolean operations. These do not alone prove absence of all self-intersections.
families.next_case: For each paired case, validate the result before and after STEP and a small downstream cut.
families.required_outcome: Deliver blend results usable for closed meshing, STEP interchange and further modeling while preserving dimensions and validity.

families.title: Actionable failures and recovery
families.occt_scope: Faulty contour/vertex queries, stripe status and optional partial result.
families.truck_scope: Structured diagnostics identify stages, selections and stations; some fallback paths retain an earlier error. Validate whether users can locate and correct a failure. An OCCT-style partial-result object is not required.
families.next_case: Mix one invalid selection into a valid operation; check that diagnostics identify the cause, the input remains intact and correction/retry succeeds.
families.required_outcome: Explain failed selections and stages clearly, preserve the model and allow the user to correct or retry a failed blend.

families.title: Invalid selections, parameters and immutable failure
families.occt_scope: Error reporting and robustness regressions, including invalid geometry.
families.truck_scope: Selection, nonfinite parameter, tolerance and input-preservation checks exist.
families.next_case: Empty/duplicate/stale edges, zero/negative/NaN sizes and nonmanifold input; no panic or input mutation.
families.required_outcome: Handle invalid, empty, duplicate or stale selections and invalid numeric parameters deterministically without panic or input mutation.

families.title: Face-driven rolling ball and stopping faces
families.occt_scope: Separate BiTgte interface permits face pairs, selected edges and stopping faces.
families.truck_scope: Existing product blends start from selected edges or face boundaries. The broader face-to-face result with stopping faces is unverified; the absence of matching methods alone is not a capability finding.
families.next_case: Use a face-pair fixture with an explicit stopping face and attempt equivalent existing constructions; judge the support contacts, termination and editable result.
families.required_outcome: Construct a round between selected support faces and terminate it at specified limiting faces, through any equivalent feature construction.

families.title: Boolean and blend composition
families.occt_scope: DRAW wrappers expose fuse/cut plus blend.
families.truck_scope: Existing Boolean and blend operations compose, with regression coverage for selected generated hole rims. A combined wrapper is not a separate feature requirement; broader intersection geometry is tracked under W03.
families.next_case: Check fuse and cut results followed by blending their intended intersection edges, including subsequent edits. Reuse W03 geometry coverage; do not add a wrapper just to match DRAW.
families.required_outcome: Fuse or cut bodies, then blend the intended resulting intersection edges while preserving the modeling intent through edits.

families.title: 2D line/arc fillets
families.occt_scope: Analytic and iterative planar fillet APIs.
families.truck_scope: Pieza has sketch corner filleting using offset/intersection candidates; separate from the 3D kernel API.
families.next_case: Line-line, line-circle and circle-circle corners, both sides, small/large radii and trimmed domains.
families.required_outcome: Round trimmed planar line/arc corners to the requested radius and chosen side, retaining connected sketch geometry.

families.title: 2D general curves and multiple solutions
families.occt_scope: Iterative fillets and solution-selection APIs cover broader curve configurations.
families.truck_scope: Complete sketch parity for spline/ellipse corners, multiple solutions and extension is unverified.
families.next_case: Exercise all fillet2d fixtures and distinguish underlying-curve solutions from trimmed-edge solutions.
families.required_outcome: Round general planar curve corners with the intended radius, trimmed domains and selected solution when several are possible.

families.title: 2D chamfers and corner edits
families.occt_scope: Planar chamfer API and fillet/chamfer modification/removal in MakeFillet2d.
families.truck_scope: A parametric sketch-chamfer workflow has not been established in the inspected code. Existing sketch edits may construct some equivalent geometry; validate dimensional intent and later edits before classifying the feature as covered or missing.
families.next_case: Create line-line chamfers with setbacks or angle, then change and remove them while retaining connectivity and constraints. Evaluate existing sketch edits as a possible equivalent route.
families.required_outcome: Create and edit planar sketch chamfers with specified setbacks or angles, maintaining connectivity and edit behavior.
